newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin against more austerity to meet EMU goals.
newsitem.headline: Jospin against more austerity to meet EMU goals.

text.p: French Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin said on Sunday he would not introduce further austerity measures to stop the public deficit overshooting the three percent target needed to join a single currency.

Jospin told TF1 television ahead of an expected snap election call: "If to respect the criteria of three percent, which Germany will probably not respect, if to do that we have to impose, with the jobless rate we have...a new austerity cure on the country my answer is no. No to the absolute respect of the three percent criterion."
Jospin proposed opening talks soon with France's partners to discuss under what conditions a single currency should go ahead.
"We will have one year to relaunch a real dialogue with Germany. We won't say yes unconditionally to monetary union if that leads to a worsening of unemployment," Jospin said.

The opposition leader said that Italy and Spain should take part in the first wave of monetary union and that there should be a European political authority, which he dubbed an "economic government", to counterbalance a future European central bank.
He added that a single European currency, due to be launched on January 1, 1999, should not be undervalued compared with the dollar.
